actions.action: Move plant to brightest spot, ideally south- or west-facing window
Increase direct sun exposure gradually to avoid burn
Take cuttings of healthy rosettes and green trailing tips
Let cut ends dry and callus for 2-3 days
Root cuttings on dry, gritty succulent mix
Root fallen leaves and baby plantlets by laying them on soil
Mist cuttings lightly or water once roots form
Check old stems for firm green parts versus dead dry ones
Unpot plant and inspect roots for die-back or rot
Repot in cactus soil with extra perlite/pumice in a pot with drainage holes
Water thoroughly and wait until soil is completely dry before watering again

reason: The answer correctly names low light as the main cause, but it treats watering as minor and even suggests underwatering instead of overwatering. Its light and soak-then-dry advice matches the fix, but it is buried under an aggressive propagation plan. Nothing it recommends would likely worsen the plant.
